source.title: Causality $\neq$ Invariance: Function and Concept Vectors in LLMs
source.authors: Gustaw Opiełka; Hannes Rosenbusch; Claire E. Stevenson

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether representations of the same relational concepts remain similar across input formats, using cosine similarity and RSA rather than measuring convergence between independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The study measures representation similarity across prompt formats and reports steering transfer across formats. Only the similarity results bear directly on the tested version; steering results do not test model-to-model interchangeability.
record.test_reason: The study compares one model's representations of the same concepts across prompt formats (Function Vectors vs Concept Vectors). It never measures alignment between independently trained models, seeds, modalities or scales, and it does not compare features across models. Its similarity results are about within-model format invariance, not representation convergence. The record's V6 link is wrong: V6 concerns how measured cross-model convergence depends on metric and inputs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that FVs mix concept with format and are causally effective, steering strongly in-distribution. RSA-selected CVs are more format-invariant, generalize more consistently out-of-distribution, but have smaller effects and are ineffective zero-shot. The two sets of heads lie in similar layers but are largely disjoint, suggesting distinct mechanisms for invariance and causality.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures concept and question-type RSA and cosine similarity across input formats, rather than measuring alignment between independently trained models as in the claim's cited sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Input format changes the measured similarity structure: FVs cluster by format while CVs cluster more by concept. RSA outcomes also differ across the tested head subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single LLM, Function Vectors for the same relational concept are nearly orthogonal across prompt formats. RSA-selected Concept Vectors cluster by concept across formats, but retain some format signal (Llama 3.1 70B: within-format cosine 0.90 for FVs vs 0.55 for CVs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model abstraction: LLM internal concept representations are (or are not) invariant to input format and language, and the components that encode invariant concepts differ from those that causally drive behaviour.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026)
record.problems: The central comparison is within models across prompt formats, not across independently trained models. Key aggregate RSA results are displayed in figures without numerical values in the text. Several reported similarity results are from Llama 3.1 70B only.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant measured results were left out.

untested.parts: Cross-model alignment and its change with scale. The four models are analysed separately and never compared.
Mapping or stitching representations between models.
Whether the same heads or features recur across models. CV/FV heads are found per model but not matched across models.
Dependence of cross-model convergence on the similarity measure or the inputs.
Degree, plateau and causes of cross-model alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mistook within-model format invariance for cross-model convergence. No result compares representations between different models, so no version of the convergence claim is tested and no verdicts are given. r1 also compares the study's own method (CVs) with a baseline (FVs).

versions.untested_parts: Scale, capability, and alignment between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions, and change with model performance.
Convergence across random seeds and shared features or subspaces between independently trained networks.
Mapping representations between different models, stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
Recurrence of the same interpretable features or circuits across different models.
The study varies input format, but does not compare a broad range of similarity measures or systematically vary similarity-measure settings such as neighbour count.
Alignment between independently trained models, plateaus with scale, and whether shared training data or objectives explain cross-model alignment.
